**Produced:** 2026-09-06 · **Gate:** `findings.md` (four passes, cleared at the 2026-09-06 adjudication)
**Base branch:** `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component` (PR #85, open, unmerged)

## 1. Goal statement

`customfield_10231`), designed in **`Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` component set `40000587:38471`**
(Desktop `40000307:12444`, Tablet `40000730:13363`, Mobile `40000538:25030` — all authoritative,
corroborated by PDP-template instances `7998:13508` / `8272:28947`), with SFCC-84's page from the

**PR #85 / SFCC-236's** `ZimmProductCard` family via a **new `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry** (not a new

recipes registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.

**Scope corrected 2026-09-07 against the real Jira AC text** (Marcel supplied the full verbatim
SFCC-83/SFCC-84 tickets; see "PLP surface" in §2 and the Open Questions for the full reconciliation).
This plan's original scope line — "follows `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4 (PDP + Cart); PLP is out;
SFCC-83 AC 9 knowingly not met" — was written against the PRD, never checked against the ticket's

are PLP, PDP, and Cart."* PLP is real, in-scope, unbuilt work — see §2.
**No consent gating** — not a development-phase carve-out awaiting a later fix, but genuinely out of
this ticket's scope: Jasmijn's own dependency note ("move the consent acceptance criteria to a
separate user story") and comment history move consent ACs to SFCC-106. Must still be stated in both
PR bodies so a reviewer doesn't read the absence as an oversight.

**🔴 Data source corrected 2026-09-08 — Einstein is confirmed "Not Deployed" on every real
Zimmermann site (Open Question 6).** By Marcel's explicit direction, this build ships against real,
live Commerce Cloud product data sourced by this browser's own tracked view history instead — see
§2's "Interim data source" for the full design. A follow-up ticket (not yet created, Open
Question 18) swaps in real Einstein later; this plan's A3/A4/A6/B2 steps are written against the
interim design already.

## 2. Scale call

### Architecture fork — resolved: override `recommended-products/`, which removes the Cart port

Verified directly at `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js`.
`isFromExtends` returns true when the request names `@salesforce/retail-react-app` **and the issuing
file is not itself inside `overrides/`**. The plugin's own comment (lines 116–127): *"This will return
true if the issuer is a file in a base template... This allow the base template to import from
overrides."* Implementation: `this.extends.includes(pkgName) && !filepath.includes(issuerPath)`.

Base Cart imports at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36`:
`import RecommendedProducts from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/recommended-products'`
— a package-path import issued from a base file, so it **is** redirected once our override exists.
Base Cart is itself loaded by base `routes.jsx` via a relative `import('./pages/cart')`, which is not
redirected — so base Cart keeps rendering and picks up our override for free.

**Consequence: the ~2,460-line Cart copy-first (`index.jsx` 1515 + 8 real partials ≈ 948) is not
required.** This departed from adjudication item #10 ("we only have to copy-first for cart"), in the
direction of *less* work. **APPROVED by Marcel, 2026-09-06**, on the evidence that this is already the
dominant pattern in this repo: nine component overrides shadow base paths and are reached purely by
the resolver (`icons` at 64 base import sites — and mandated by AGENTS.md — `responsive` 12,
`product-view` 6, `drawer-menu`/`list-menu` 2 each, `header`/`footer` 1 each). The single page port
(`product-detail`) exists only because base `routes.jsx` loads pages by *relative* import, which the
resolver never redirects — a constraint that does not apply to components. Open Question 5 is closed.

**Caveat:** this is a *build-time webpack* resolver. It runs in the dev server and production build
only — **not** Storybook (`.storybook/main.js` aliases straight to `node_modules`) and **not** Vitest.
So the Cart behaviour cannot be proven by any automated test in this repo; it must be checked in the
running app. That is why A1's pause is a hard gate.

Cost of this choice: the override module loads at **four base import sites serving eight rails**, not
five as an earlier draft of this plan stated:

| Base import site | Rails | Takes the new branch? |
|---|---|---|
| `app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36` | Cart Recently Viewed, Cart May-Also-Like | **Yes** (1 of 2) |
| `app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx:40` | *(shadowed by our own PDP override — 3 rails)* | **Yes** (1 of 3) |
| `app/hooks/use-add-to-cart-modal.js:30` | add-to-cart modal (`pdp-similar-items`) | No |
| `app/pages/product-list/partials/empty-results.jsx:20` | PLP empty-search top-sellers, most-viewed | No |

It is therefore a **faithful port plus exactly one branch**, keyed off
`EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` (`'viewed-recently-einstein'` — the same string as
`CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED`, `constants.js:156,160`). **Two rails take the new branch; the other six must
render identically before and after** — a hard pass criterion.

**🔴 Correction, 2026-09-06 — the PDP row above is misleading, verified directly against
`overrides-plugin.js`'s actual source, not just this plan's earlier paraphrase of it.** The
table's "Yes (1 of 3)" for `product-detail/index.jsx:40` describes the **base** file's import —
but that file is shadowed by our own PDP override page and never loads. What actually matters is
*our own* `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`'s import of `RecommendedProducts`, and
`isFromExtends` (`overrides-plugin.js:128-146`) returns **false** whenever the issuing file is
itself inside `overrides/` — its own doc comment says so plainly: *"This will return false if the
issuer is a file in the overrides dir."* Our PDP page's current package-path import
(`product-detail/index.tsx:59`) is therefore **not** redirected to our override, at all, regardless
of `Island`, scroll position, or Einstein data — none of which were ever the actual blocker.
Discovered live during A1's mandatory Cart/PDP verification (Marcel: zero marker fires on PDP even
after a full scroll to the bottom, while Cart fired correctly and repeatedly).

**Consequence, and why this isn't just a testing nuisance:** as originally planned, PDP's Recently
Viewed rail would never render even after A6 lands the branch — Cart would work, PDP would
silently not, and SFCC-83's PDP requirement would ship broken with no test catching it (no PR-time
E2E on this path either, per the Loop depth section below). **Fix, folded into A6 (Marcel,
2026-09-06):** change `product-detail/index.tsx:59`'s `RecommendedProducts` import from the base
package path to a relative path pointing at our own override, per
`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s existing "Importing an already-overridden component from a
new component" rule — the exact same doctrine
A6 already applies to `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` below, just missed for `RecommendedProducts` itself
in the original draft of this plan. See A6's updated step and pass criteria.

Two of those six are on **PLP**, explicitly descoped at adjudication #2. The override *loads* there
but its branch never fires (those rails use `EMPTY_SEARCH_RESULTS_*` recommenders), so **no Recently
Viewed rail appears on PLP**. State this in the PR body so a reviewer does not read the override's
presence on PLP as scope creep.

Rejected alternative — re-homing the fetch into a new Zimmermann container: still needs a per-surface
caller, and Cart is a base page we cannot pass props to without the 2,460-line port. Buys nothing,
costs the port.

### Branch: ONE, single PR (Marcel, 2026-09-06)

**`feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed`**, cut from `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`.

An earlier draft proposed two stacked branches. **Marcel chose a single branch / single PR to
maintain**, which is now the plan. Step IDs keep their `A*`/`B*` prefixes (they read as "rail work"
and "page work") but execute as one sequence on one branch:

> A1 → A2 → A3 → A4 → A5 → A6 → B1 → B2 → B3 → GATES

**What this buys:**
- **The AC 5 / AC 84-1 split disappears.** Those two ACs are the *same* requirement. On two branches
  the rail would have shipped with an unsupplied `seeAllHref` and SFCC-83 could not be marked Done
  until the second PR merged. On one branch the link and its destination land together — no
  interim state where the link points at a 404, and both stories close on one merge.
- One review conversation, one CI run, one changelog entry.

**What it costs, stated plainly:**
- **The four-team CODEOWNERS fan-out on `overrides/app/routes.tsx` (`CODEOWNERS:94`) now applies to
  the whole PR**, not just the page half. Every reviewer group sees the full diff.
- **The provisional-design page now gates the confirmed-design rail.** SFCC-83's rail is authoritative
  at all three viewports and corroborated twice; SFCC-84's page comes entirely from a provisional
  source. If the page's design is challenged in review, the rail — which re-skins two live surfaces
  and has no such doubt — waits with it. Accepted deliberately; flag it in the PR body so a reviewer
  knows the rail can be split back out if the page stalls.

### Loop depth

Two stories, ~22 files, one 236-line copy-first file. Mid-size build.

- **Full implementer → tester → scorer** on A2, A3, A4, A5, B1, B3 — where a silent wrong answer
  ships (a variation flag misread from Figma; an ordering/cap bug of exactly the shape the FED
  handbook's finding 18 warns encodes itself into a passing test; an AC-8 gate that never fires).
- **Implementer + scorer only** on A1, A6, B2, A7, B4 — their gate is mechanical (`tsc`, `npm run
  test`, a diff read); a tester pass adds a round-trip without adding a check.

**Deliberately dropped, with reasons:**
- **No Playwright/E2E.** Adding an allow-list group to `.github/workflows/qa.yml` is Tier 1 CI config
  (`CODEOWNERS:65`) — out of scope. Without it these paths resolve to `e2e_scope: skip` and there is
  no PR-time E2E run either way (`.claude/rules/testing.md` > Change-scoped E2E). State this in both
  PR bodies rather than implying coverage exists.
- **No page-level Storybook story.** No page in this repo has one; the presentational organisms carry
  the stories, matching `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/*.stories.tsx`.
- **No new `theme/components/*Shared.ts`.** Both recipes derive media queries from `breakpoints`
  imported from `app/theme/foundation` — one source, two importers, no copied literal.
- **No visual-regression tooling.** None exists; Figma parity is checked by eye against named nodes.

### PLP surface — 🟢 DECIDED 2026-09-08 (Marcel): fold into this single PR

**Superseded, not refined.** This plan's original scope line ("PLP is out; SFCC-83 AC 9 knowingly
not met") was written against `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4's "PDP + Cart" framing and never checked
against the ticket's own AC text. Marcel supplied the full verbatim SFCC-83 ticket 2026-09-07; its
AC states plainly: *"Confirmed surfaces are PLP, PDP, and Cart."* PLP is real, in-scope, unbuilt
work, not a knowingly-deferred gap — the earlier "Routed, not planned into" note calling AC 9
wrong-as-written (bottom of this document) is itself the thing that was wrong, and is corrected
there.

**What's missing.** Unlike PDP and Cart, PLP has no existing base call site rendering a
`RecommendedProducts`-style rail keyed to `EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` /
`'viewed-recently-einstein'`. The two PLP-side consumers this plan's own architecture-fork table
already identified (`product-list/partials/empty-results.jsx`'s top-sellers/most-viewed rails) use
the `EMPTY_SEARCH_RESULTS_*` recommenders instead, and only render on an empty search — not the
general "you've been browsing" placement PLP needs. This means PLP needs a **new call site**, not a
branch inside an existing one — most likely a new `RecommendedProducts` usage added to
`overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx` or a `product-list/partials/` file. That path is
**Squad A territory** per `.claude/rules/squadA.md` — a different owner than every other file this
plan touches (all Squad B / shared so far), and that rule file requires notifying the Squad A Lead
before touching it.

**Not designed yet.** No Figma node in either the original set or Marcel's 2026-09-07 supply is
confirmed as "Recently Viewed on PLP" specifically — the closest candidates are the unread
`Zimmermann_Designs` `9086:*` family (see Open Question 15, pending Figma auth). Placement (top of
grid? after N rows? sidebar?) is undetermined.

**Decided 2026-09-08 (Marcel): "we're doing PLP as well."** Folds into this single PR, not a
fast-follow. This does expand the file manifest into a fourth owner and a page tier this plan
hadn't touched (Squad A pages) — the "spans multiple protection tiers" condition AGENTS.md Hard
Rule #10 flags — but the decision itself is now made; add a real file-manifest row (below) and
notify the Squad A Lead per `squadA.md` before touching `product-list/`.

**Still genuinely open: exact placement.** No Figma node anywhere in the supplied set is confirmed
as "Recently Viewed on PLP" specifically — not designed yet, not guessed here. Mechanically, the
new call site is a `<RecommendedProducts recommender={EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED}
.../>` added to `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx` (or a `product-list/partials/` file,
if the eventual placement sits inside an existing partial rather than the page shell) — the same
mechanical pattern PDP/Cart already use, wired through the same interim data source as A6 (§2). The
open question is purely *where in the page* (top of grid? after N rows? sidebar?), not whether or
how it's wired. **Owner: Marcel — confirm placement before this specific file is written**, though
nothing else in this PR needs to wait on it.

### Interim data source — Einstein unavailable, ship against real browser-tracked history (Marcel, 2026-09-08)

**Why this exists.** Einstein is confirmed "Not Deployed" on every real Zimmermann site (see Open

the whole build on a platform-provisioning timeline outside this team's control, Marcel directed:
ship the UI now against **real, live Commerce Cloud product data**, sourced by **this browser's own
actual view history**, tracked client-side — not Einstein, and not any hardcoded/mocked fixture

  never read; the new history hook + a real `getProducts` call are used instead.
- **B2** — same swap: the page container calls the new history hook instead of
  `getRecommendations`, and feeds the stored ID list (**capped at 24, not the rail's 5-item
  slice** — see the stored-history-cap note below, superseded from an earlier "full, uncapped"
  framing once the `getProducts` 24-ID limit was discovered) into the richer was/now/multi-image
  mapper already planned.

**Storage mechanics, per "browser/local it is":**
- **Guests:** `sessionStorage` — unchanged from A4's existing design, still correctly satisfies AC 6

- **Registered shoppers:** `localStorage` — a genuine, explicit, temporary deviation from both AC 7

  called out plainly in the PR body and to whoever signs off testing, not discovered by a confused

  single device and called passing.

- **Stored-history cap — RESOLVED 2026-09-08, then SUPERSEDED same day once the 24-ID fetch limit
  was discovered.** Original reasoning (Marcel: "how would this be treated if Einstein were
  available? do the same as that"): real Einstein has no client-supplied "how far back to
  remember" parameter, so this isn't a product/UX decision — `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED =

  is now incomplete, not wrong** — it was correct given what was known at the time, but didn't yet

  found the contradiction between what it was told to build and what this section said, and
  correctly surfaced it rather than silently picking a side — exactly the discipline this plan
  asks for elsewhere. **Open Question 17 is re-closed at the new number** — no further confirmation
  needed; this is a direct, logical consequence of Marcel's own 24-cap decision, not a new
  independent judgement call.

**What stays exactly as planned, unaffected by this whole section:** A2 (variation config), A5 (rail
UI), B1 (grid UI) — all purely presentational, receive cards as props, and have never cared where
those props came from. This is the container/presentational split (`components.md`) paying off
exactly as designed.

**To verify at implementation time, not guessed here:** the exact `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`
hook name for a batch product-detail fetch (likely `useProducts`, plural, alongside the already-used
singular `useProduct` — confirm against `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/dist/` per AGENTS.md's
own Gotchas note before trusting the name).

**Not a scope decision for this PR:** what the Einstein follow-up ticket looks like in detail (does

### A4 — Recently-viewed history hook, plus the PDP write

**🔴 REVISED 2026-09-08 — renamed and re-designed, per "Interim data source" in §2. Read this whole
step before implementing; the original boolean logic below is no longer correct and would ship a
real bug if built as originally specced.**

Create `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts` (was `useRecentlyViewedGate.ts`).

This still answers **finding 28** — the *original* concern was that Einstein's recommender returns a
two-product baseline for a visitor with zero history, so `recs.length === 0` never fires and AC 8
isn't implementable from the response. With Einstein out of the picture for this build, that specific
failure mode can't happen either way (there is no Einstein response to leak a baseline from) — but
the fix is still needed, now for a more basic reason: something has to track what "recently viewed"
even means without Einstein.

**The boolean logic changes, not just the storage mechanism — this is the one real gotcha in this
revision.** The original design was:

```
hasRecentlyViewed = sessionFlagIsSet || isRegistered
```

`isRegistered` was a deliberate short-circuit: trust that a logged-in shopper has *some* server-side
Einstein history even on a fresh device. **That assumption breaks entirely once Einstein is out of
the loop** — there is no server-side history to trust anymore. Built as originally specced, every
registered shopper would show `hasRecentlyViewed = true` unconditionally, including one who has
never viewed anything in this interim system on any device — gating the rail *open* with zero real
cards behind it. That's a real, shippable bug, not a hypothetical; it must not be carried into the
interim build. **Corrected logic:**

```
hasRecentlyViewed = recentlyViewedIds.length > 0
```

— true for both guests and registered shoppers alike, based purely on this interim system's own
tracked history. `isRegistered` still matters, just for a different purpose now: it selects *which*
storage to read/write (see below), not whether to bypass the check.

**New return shape:** `{hasRecentlyViewed: boolean, recentlyViewedIds: readonly string[],
markProductViewed: (productId: string) => void}` — the boolean is now derived from the ID list, not
tracked independently, so the two can never disagree.

- `markProductViewed(productId)` writes to `sessionStorage` (guest) or `localStorage` (registered,
  via `isRegistered` from `useCustomerType()` — the same hook `use-einstein.js:449` already uses) —
  called from the existing Einstein `useEffect` in
  `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (lines 772–801), alongside the
  `einstein.sendViewProduct` calls already there (left untouched — that call is unrelated real
  analytics, not this build's concern). One import, one call, guarded by the same `if (product)`.
- **De-duplication / move-to-front:** if `productId` is already in the stored list, remove the old
  entry before prepending — never a duplicate, and a re-view correctly becomes "most recent" again.
- **Cap the stored list** at `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED` (**24, superseded from an earlier
  500 same day — see §2** — matches the Full History page's own 24-ID fetch cap, since nothing
  beyond item 24 is ever displayable) — trim from the tail, oldest-first, on write.

**AC mapping, restated for the interim system:** `sessionStorage` is session-scoped and cleared at
session end — **AC 6**, unchanged. **AC 7 (cross-device for registered shoppers) is explicitly
*not* satisfied by this interim design** — `localStorage` is still device-local. This must be stated
plainly in the PR body and marked N/A-pending-the-Einstein-follow-up for this specific AC, not tested
against a single device and reported as passing. See §2's "Interim data source" for the full
reasoning — this is a stated, accepted gap, not an oversight.

**Confirmed 2026-09-07, not a frontend gap** (pre-dates and is unaffected by this revision — restated
for continuity): SFCC-83's own Assumptions section states *"the storage of Recently Viewed is
handled by SFCC."* The interim system above is a **temporary, explicit stand-in** for that
assumption while Einstein is unavailable, not a rejection of it — once the Einstein follow-up lands,
this hook's job reverts to a thin boolean/gate again and the real history moves back server-side, per
the original design intent this section used to describe.

**Superseded by the above, not applicable to the interim build:** the old "stated assumption" about
a registered shopper with genuinely zero Einstein history still seeing a two-product baseline
(Open Question 6's original framing) — that residual was specific to trusting Einstein's own
baseline behaviour, which the interim system never calls, so it cannot leak through here. It returns
once the Einstein follow-up is built, at which point Open Question 6's original text applies again.
